title: Move WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter to a SecurityFilterChain
summary: The security config is rewritten for Boot 3, then a new role goes in below a broader rule that catches it first.

turns.user: upgraded to boot 3 and SecurityConfig does not compile. says WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter does not exist

assistant.body: Note: WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter was deprecated in Spring Security 5.7 and removed in 6.0, which is what Boot 3 uses. The replacement is a @Bean that takes HttpSecurity and returns a SecurityFilterChain. Along the way authorizeRequests became authorizeHttpRequests and antMatchers became requestMatchers. Chaining with and() is deprecated as of 6.1 too, so this is written in the lambda DSL.

turns.user: works. now /api/admin/reports/** should also be open to the AUDITOR role

assistant.body: Sure. One line for reports goes right after the admin rule. hasAnyRole adds the ROLE_ prefix itself, so it takes bare role names.

turns.user: logged in as an AUDITOR and /api/admin/reports/daily gives me 403

assistant.body: Apologies, I got the order wrong. authorizeHttpRequests checks its rules top to bottom and uses the first one that matches. /api/admin/reports/daily matches /api/admin/** first, gets judged by hasRole("ADMIN") there, and never reaches the line below. Best practice: narrow rules before broad ones. It is the same reason anyRequest has to come last, or the app fails at startup.

turns.user: ops also wants actuator info without auth. just add it next to health right

assistant.body: Yes, one more path on the permitAll line. Keep in mind Boot 3 only exposes health over the web by default, so check that management.endpoints.web.exposure.include lists info as well.
